summary: This rerun is a large, genuine improvement over the previous round, and almost everything is now proven on the real deployed app. I opened all eleven images and the storage transcript. Ten images are captures of the changed application at the run-owned temporary Worker origin https://deos-tmp-707e60c64357d9e1197de094.skundu.workers.dev/, and one is the required local loopback smoke check at http://127.0.0.1:8787/ which additionally shows the honest "Snippets could not be loaded. Try again." load-failure banner. The images are all visually distinct and internally consistent (banner text, snippet counts, reader contents), so nothing looks like a fixture or a reused screenshot, which was the previous round's main defect. The storage proof is now raw rather than prose: scripts/verify-remote-storage.mjs is a frozen source that simply replays saved request files through the trusted runtime and prints the provider result verbatim, and it shows a genuinely empty baseline (0 snippets, 0 operations, no R2 objects, GET /api/snippets returning {"snippets":[]}) and a final readback with real D1 metadata, the exact object_key and body_sha256 for Greeting and Markup sample, the full R2 key listing, and byte-level readbacks "Hello, team!" and "Hello". The arithmetic ties out: 100 active rows, reserved_bytes 122 = 98 one-byte capacity fixtures + 12 + 12, and one deleted operation holding zero reserved bytes, which is the Sign-off tombstone; Overflow and "Empty note" both have zero rows, so the rejected saves wrote nothing. Code review confirms the app really uses env.DB (D1), env.BODIES (R2) and ASSETS.fetch, and renders titles and bodies through text nodes. One gap remains and it repeats an unaddressed item from the previous review: the plan's failed-action scenario was never demonstrated. There is no browser proof of a failed read or a failed delete through the deployed app, so the approved "Report failed actions" requirement is only half shown (a real failed save is shown by the capacity rejection, and a failed load by the local smoke check, but the spec's "Report a failed delete" scenario is evidenced only by vitest, and the plan itself said tests are not demonstrations). The app code at src/web/app.js already contains the exact read-failure and delete-reconciliation messages, so this is an evidence gap, not a code gap, and it is reachable with the declared capabilities by deleting one prepared snippet out-of-band through the app's own API and then acting on the stale page. Applying the later human answers: the 2026-09-17 16:57 instruction to use the adjacent fresh-browser scenario against unchanged cloud data is now satisfied, and the 2026-09-18 07:51 comment moves removal of the temporary infrastructure to the normal workflow after the PR is updated, so I did not require a removal receipt from the implementer, and it also requires exactly the local-plus-remote split that was delivered. One incidental note for the human reviewer: an earlier "npm run check" run exited 1 on a single api.test.ts case, but the same test was rerun green and a later full "npm test" exited 0, so it reads as a flake rather than a defect. No requirement was weakened and no new requirement was added.
